metadata.scenario_context: A group of software engineers working remotely for a global tech company decides to initiate a team-building meeting early in January. Luis raises the idea of going on a strike to protest against some changes from the company's management.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Spain strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Ecuador strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Suggest the possibility of scheduling the team-building meeting on January 1st.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss a specific date for the team-building meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Javier
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Ahmed, I was thinking... what if we schedule the team-building meeting on January 1st? It could be a good way to start the new year together. 

Also, I'm curious— is it common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest in our industry? I just... I don't really see that happening in Spain.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
January 1st? Hmm... that's New Year's Day, so many people might be busy with family or celebrations. Maybe we should think about a date later in January? 

As for strikes... in Ecuador, we generally don’t participate in strikes. It’s not something that’s seen as common or effective for us. It’s more about finding solutions through discussion, you know?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Javier
shared_prefix.message:
I get that, but starting the year with a team-building meeting could really set a positive tone. I think it’s worth considering. 

And about strikes, that’s interesting... I mean, I just feel like in Spain, we usually find other ways to express our views. Strikes seem a bit extreme to me. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message: I see your point about the team-building meeting setting a positive tone, and that’s definitely important. But, you know, when it comes to strikes, I think we can find common ground. People are pretty much motivated by the same things, and I believe that underneath we are the same. Whether in Spain or Ecuador, expressing views can be done in various ways. It’s just about finding the right approach that suits everyone. Maybe we can explore other forms of expression together?
